newsitem.title: MONACO: SOCCER-MONACO BEAT LILLE TO OPEN 13-POINT LEAD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MONACO BEAT LILLE TO OPEN 13-POINT LEAD.

text.p: Monaco opened a commanding 13-point lead in the French first division after cruising to a 2-0 victory over 10-man Lille on Friday.
With just nine games to play second-placed Paris St. Germain must now beat Rennes at the Parc des Princes on Saturday to maintain their already slim title hopes.
After a lacklustre first half the game changed on the hour with the sending-off of Lille's Cedric Carrez. Monaco cashed in with goals by Nigeria's Viktor Ikpeba and midfielder Sylvain Legwinski.
The match was a gentle warm-up for Monaco's UEFA Cup semifinal first leg against Italy's Internazionale next Tuesday.
Lille, who are fighting to avoid relegation, cracked after defender Carrez was sent off for a bad foul on Brazilian striker Sonny Anderson.
Anderson had missed a penalty in the 44th minute in the only notable action of the first half.
The red card changed the match and a minute later Ilpeba headed in Ali Benarbia's corner.
Eight minutes later Legwinski made it two with a superb shot from the edge of the box. Monaco then relaxed, saving their energy for Tuesday.
The defeat completed a miserable day for Lille following the news that midfielder David Garcion had been suspended for 18 months for taking steroids.
They are fourth-from-bottom in the league having played more games than all their rivals.
